title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 1:1
body: “Wherefore then, when writing to the Ephesians, and having Timothy with him, did he not include him with himself (in his salutation), known as he was to them and admired, for he says, "Ye know the proof of him, that as a child serveth the father, so he served with me in the Gospel" (Philip.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 1
bodyEs: “¿Por qué, pues, al escribir a los efesios, y teniendo consigo a Timoteo, no lo incluyó consigo (en su saludo), siendo conocido de ellos y admirado, pues dice: «la experiencia de él habéis conocido, que como hijo á padre ha servido conmigo en el evangelio» (Filip.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 1:8
body: “As a sweet-smelling ointment keeps not its fragrance shut up in itself, but diffuses it afar, and scenting the air with its perfume, so conveys it also to the senses of the neighbors; so too illustrious and admirable men do not shut up their virtue within themselves, but by their good report benefit many, and render them better. Which also then happened.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 2
bodyEs: “Como un ungüento de olor dulce no guarda su fragancia encerrada en sí mismo, sino que la difunde lejos, y perfumando el aire con su aroma, así lo lleva también a los sentidos de los vecinos; así también los hombres ilustres y admirables no encierran su virtud dentro de sí mismos, sino que con su buen nombre benefician a muchos y los hacen mejores. Lo cual sucedió también entonces.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 2:9
body: “The teacher ought to do nothing with a feeling of being burdened, that tends to the salvation of his disciples. For if the blessed Jacob was buffeted night and day in keeping his flocks, much more ought he, to whom the care of souls is entrusted, to endure all toils, though the work be laborious and mean, looking only to one thing, the salvation of his disciples, and the glory thence arising to God.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 3
bodyEs: “El maestro no debe hacer nada con sentimiento de carga, de lo que tiende a la salvación de sus discípulos. Porque si el bienaventurado Jacob fue golpeado noche y día al guardar sus rebaños, mucho más debe el que tiene confiado el cuidado de las almas soportar todos los trabajos, aunque la obra sea laboriosa y humilde, mirando solo a una cosa: la salvación de sus discípulos, y la gloria que de ahí sube a Dios.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 3:5
body: “A question lies before us to-day, which is much disputed, and which is gathered from many sources. But what is this question?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 4
bodyEs: “Hoy tenemos delante una cuestión muy disputada, y que se recoge de muchas fuentes. Pero ¿cuál es esta cuestión?”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 4:1
body: “When he has met what was pressing, and what was upon his hands, and is about henceforth to enter upon things that are perpetual, and which they ought continually to hear, he adds this expression, "finally," that is, always and forever. "We beseech and exhort you in the Lord." Strange!”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 5
bodyEs: “Cuando ha atendido lo que apremiaba, y lo que tenía entre manos, y está a punto de entrar en cosas que son perpetuas, y que ellos debían oír de continuo, añade esta expresión, «Resta pues», esto es, siempre y para siempre. «Os roguemos y exhortemos en el Señor». ¡Extraño!”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 4:9
body: “Why then having discoursed with them earnestly concerning chastity, and being about to discourse about the duty of working, and about the not sorrowing for the departed, does he introduce that which was the principal of all good things, love, as if he were passing it over, saying, "We have no need to write to you"? This also is from his great wisdom, and belongs to spiritual instruction.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 6
bodyEs: “¿Por qué, pues, habiendo discurrido con ellos con empeño acerca de la castidad, y estando a punto de discurrir acerca del deber de trabajar, y de no entristecerse por los que han partido, introduce aquello que era lo principal de todas las cosas buenas, el amor, como si lo pasara por alto, diciendo: «no habéis menester que os escriba»? Esto también es de su gran sabiduría, y pertenece a la instrucción espiritual.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 4:13
body: “There are many things which from ignorance alone cause us sorrow, so that if we come to understand them well, we banish our grief. This therefore Paul also showing, says, "I would not have you ignorant, that ye sorrow not, even as the rest, which have no hope." Is it on this account thou wouldest not have them ignorant?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 7
bodyEs: “Hay muchas cosas que solo por ignorancia nos causan tristeza, de modo que, si llegamos a entenderlas bien, desterramos nuestro dolor. Esto, pues, lo muestra también Pablo, y dice: «no queremos que ignoréis… que no os entristezcáis como los otros que no tienen esperanza». ¿Es por esto que no quieres que ignoren?”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 5:1
body: “Nothing, as it seems, is so curious, and so fondly prone to pry into things obscure and concealed, as the nature of men. And this is wont to happen to it, when the mind is unsettled and in an imperfect state.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 9
bodyEs: “Nada, según parece, es tan curioso, ni tan aficionado a husmear en las cosas oscuras y escondidas, como la naturaleza de los hombres. Y esto suele sucederle cuando la mente está inquieta y en un estado imperfecto.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 5:12
body: “It must needs happen that a ruler should have many occasions of enmities. As physicians are compelled to give much trouble to the sick, preparing for them both diet and medicines that are not pleasant indeed, but attended with benefit; and as fathers are often annoying to their children: so also are teachers, and much more.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 10
bodyEs: “Por fuerza ha de suceder que un gobernante tenga muchas ocasiones de enemistades. Como los médicos se ven obligados a dar mucha molestia a los enfermos, preparándoles tanto dieta como medicinas que no son agradables, sí, pero van acompañadas de beneficio; y como los padres a menudo fastidian a sus hijos: así también los maestros, y mucho más.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Thessalonians 5:19
body: “A thick mist, a darkness and cloud is spread over all the earth. And, showing this, the Apostle said, "For we were once darkness." (Eph.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 11
bodyEs: “Una niebla espesa, una oscuridad y una nube se extienden sobre toda la tierra. Y, mostrando esto, el apóstol dijo: «en otro tiempo erais tinieblas». (Ef.”
